title: Review of physical action execution refactor
rationale: The proposed physical-action path directly calls an adapter without deterministic Guardrails or the Executor, loses idempotency across restart, and treats a missing observation timestamp as fresh. These are reachable physical-safety failures. Required named simulation, restart, failure-injection, rollback, and supervised hardware evidence is also unavailable, so the reported generic fake-adapter CI cannot support approval.
scope_architecture: The three changed modules are within the stated watering-execution and freshness scope, but the implementation does not satisfy the architecture boundary. app/control.py performs adapter I/O itself, app/executor.py supplies only process-local deduplication rather than an idempotent state machine, and app/guardrails.py fails open on missing freshness data. The brief also omits an explicit abort/rollback boundary and the applicable failure-regression mapping required for a high-risk physical-action change.

findings.finding: The control function sends watering directly to the adapter, bypassing deterministic Guardrails and the Executor.
findings.evidence: The added water branch invokes adapter.water directly and contains no Guardrails decision or Executor transition.
findings.impact: An unvalidated suggestion can cause a real watering action without freshness, bounds, confidence, audit, idempotency, or safe-failure enforcement.
findings.required_change: Route every candidate action through deterministic Guardrails and an idempotent Executor using an approved or fake adapter; Control must not perform adapter I/O.
findings.suggested_test: Simulate allowed and rejected watering candidates through the complete Control-to-Guardrails-to-Executor-to-fake-adapter path and assert no adapter call on invalid, stale, missing, or low-confidence input.

findings.finding: Execution idempotency exists only in process memory and a send is marked acknowledged without durable acknowledgement state.
findings.evidence: ACKNOWLEDGED is a module-level set; execute sends first and then adds the identifier to that volatile set. Restart clears it, and no durable pending, uncertain, or acknowledged transition is recorded.
findings.impact: Redelivery after restart can repeat watering, while a timeout or uncertain acknowledgement can be falsely treated as safely completed.
findings.required_change: Persist idempotency keys and explicit execution transitions before/after adapter interaction, and fail safe for timeout, restart, uncertain state, and late acknowledgement.
findings.suggested_test: Simulate duplicate delivery, process restart, timeout, late acknowledgement, and storage failure with one command identifier and assert at-most-once physical dispatch plus an observable safe state.

findings.finding: A state with no observed_at timestamp is assigned age zero and therefore accepted as fresh.
findings.evidence: The conditional expression uses 0 when observed_at is absent, and the following comparison accepts that value.
findings.evidence_excerpt:
age_seconds = (now - state["observed_at"]).total_seconds() if state.get("observed_at") else 0
return age_seconds <= 300
findings.impact: Missing or unknown-age telemetry can authorize a physical watering action instead of failing safe.
findings.required_change: Reject missing, malformed, future, naive/incompatible, or stale timestamps and use an explicit timezone-aware UTC freshness check before authorization.
findings.suggested_test: Test missing, null, malformed, future, timezone-naive, boundary-age, and stale observed_at values and assert only valid timezone-aware fresh state is accepted.

findings.finding: Required physical-action simulation, restart/failure-injection, supervised hardware, and availability rehearsal evidence is missing.
findings.evidence: The report states only generic unit/fake-adapter CI and explicitly records the supervised safe-hardware and restart rehearsal as not run; it does not identify the mandatory duplicate, retry, timeout, late-acknowledgement, restart, stale, Guardrails, storage-failure, abort, or rollback checks.
findings.evidence_excerpt: NOT RUN: supervised safe-hardware and restart rehearsal
findings.impact: The high-risk exit criteria remain open, so neither safe physical behavior nor recoverability is established even if generic CI passed.
findings.required_change: Provide PASS evidence for every required deterministic fake-path check and an explicit human-owned safe-hardware, abort, rollback, and restart rehearsal, or keep the change unapproved until that evidence exists.
findings.suggested_test: manual: Run the approved supervised safe-hardware and restart/rollback procedure with a human safety owner, bounded action, manual abort, and recorded post-rollback health.

contract_consumer_review: The proposed command/suggestion fields have no explicit version, units, ranges, identifier semantics, producer, or consumer list. The adapter path bypasses the required cross-owner Control candidate -> Guardrails -> Executor contract, and the command identifier is not shown to persist across restart. No old/current replay or approved edge-adapter compatibility evidence is supplied.

evidence_matrix.check: SHA-256 verification for all three supplied patch artifacts
Reported generic unit tests and fake-adapter CI
Full baseline pytest, lint, format, and type checks
Named Guardrails, duplicate, retry, timeout, late-acknowledgement, restart, stale/low-confidence, and storage-failure simulations
Architecture and fail-safe inspection of the supplied execution path
Supervised safe-hardware, abort, restart, and rollback evidence

operations_safety_security_privacy: The patch is unsafe for physical execution: it creates a direct adapter path, volatile deduplication, false acknowledgement semantics, and fail-open freshness. There is no bounded retry/timeout policy, durable audit transition, storage-failure behavior, manual override, abort boundary, rollback owner, or post-restart health evidence. No production access or real hardware was used during this review.
documentation_assessment: No versioned action contract, operator procedure, abort/rollback instruction, or current-state update is included. The brief's claim that repeated commands and freshness are handled safely is contradicted by the patch, and its high-risk evidence plan is incomplete.
limitations: Review was limited to the approved case brief, implementation report, governing context pack, and the three hash-verified supplied patches.
No runtime source outside the supplied patches, CI logs, hardware evidence, production infrastructure, or production secrets were inspected.
